text:
maria (product): FYI — followup from yesterday's RFC review. We're seeing dashboard renders spike when RBAC checks happen per-panel. thinking about an "authorization windowing" approach to reduce repeated checks across widgets.

jon (eng): do you have numbers? is this authz CPU-bound or latency-bound?

maria (product): quick summary from trace sampling: median render 230ms, p95 ~1.7s. authz cluster of calls adds ~400ms p95. panels often trigger identical tenant+user checks.

sam (observability): confirmed from traces — many small auth requests show up as separate spans. partial aggregation in traces: 8–20 auth spans per dashboard page.

devon (infra): what's current flow? each panel asks authz service for permission for its resource id? no caching?

tess (runtime): yes — current console query layer calls authz for each panel row/visual. There is a tiny LRU in front but TTL is 1s and high cardinality kills it.

jon (eng): idea: batch authz at the query-layer boundary — compute the union of resource ids for the whole page, call authz once with that set, then distribute results back per-panel. reduces RPCs and allows single cache lookup.

maria (product): that aligns with "windowing" idea: open a short-lived window for a render request, dedupe checks, and fallback to per-panel checks if window misses. tradeoffs?

devon (infra): concerns: set-based authz pushes larger payloads to the service and changes authz API shape (list -> list). also needs authz service paging/limits if huge pages.

tess (runtime): implementation sketch: at request start, intercept the render plan, collect resource keys (limit N=1024), call `/batch_check` with resource list + user token, memoize results for request lifecycle. If list too big, fall back to streaming per-panel.

sam (observability): we should add request-level sampling flags and metrics: window_hit, window_miss, batch_size, cpu_ms_saved. Need to see p50/p95 improvements before rollout.

jon (eng): also need to think about stale decisions: if we memoize for request only that's fine. But some customers want longer memoization (session-level) to reduce rechecks across invites/updates — that's a separate opt-in feature.

maria (product): product constraint: audits must be preserved. any batching must produce audit events per original resource check (not just aggregated).

devon (infra): authz-bot: "audit: batch_check invoked for user=uid-42 resources=12" — we can have authz service emit one audit line per batch element. slight increase in log write but necessary.

authz-bot: audit: batch_check user=uid-42 size=12 duration_ms=7

tess (runtime): perf estimate from local microbench: single batch call for 50 items ~ 12ms vs 50 single calls ~ 220ms (RPC overhead). even with serialization, batch looks promising.

jon (eng): rollout plan proposal: feature-flag gated, route 10% of console traffic through batch-windowing, collect metrics for 2w, increase to 50% if p95 latency reduces and no regression in audit.

sam (observability): can add tracing tag `authz.windowed=true/false` and dashboard. also fail-open policy during rollout in case authz service returns 5xx (i.e., default to per-panel checks). need an incident playbook entry.

maria (product): ok can own product signoff. devon, can you coordinate API change with authz team? tess/jon to prototype in query-layer. sam to build dashboard.

devon (infra): will ping authz owners and propose minimal `/batch_check` contract (ids: [string], user: string, return map[id]->allow/deny + per-id audit tokens).

tess (runtime): will start a branch — rough ETA 1 sprint for prototype. will post PR and perf numbers.

jon (eng): one more: watch for amplification when panels request derived resources (e.g., panel asks for row-level subkeys). we should canonicalize keys at planner stage to keep batch size small.

maria (product): good call. let's keep keys coarse-first and fall back to fine-grained only when necessary.

sam (observability): adding a quick query to discover top N dashboards by authz RPC count — will share in #eng-platform in ~30m.

maria (product): thanks all. feels like a clear next step. tagging this thread for the RFC followup doc. :thumbsup:
